claim: Herrenchiemsee New Palace and King Ludwig II Museum are open 1 April-24 October 9:00-18:00 (last admission 17:00); 25 October-31 March 10:00-16:45 (last admission 15:45).
quote: April-24 October: 9 am-6 pm (last admission at 5 pm); 25 October-March: 10 am-4.45 pm (last admission at 3.45 pm)

claim: The Herrenchiemsee Island combination ticket (New Palace + Ludwig II Museum + Augustinian Monastery) costs €11 / €10 reduced; children under 18 free; visits to the New Palace are only possible on a ~40-minute guided tour, while the Ludwig II Museum is self-guided.
quote: Combination ticket "Island" ... 11 euros regular, 10 euros reduced ... Children under 18 are admitted free of charge ... visit to the New Palace is only possible with a guided tour (approximately 40 minutes)

claim: Chiemsee-Schifffahrt operates year-round ferries from Prien/Stock and Gstadt to Herreninsel and Fraueninsel, with the trip from Prien-Stock to Herreninsel taking about 20 minutes.
quote: 365 days service from the ports Prien/Stock and Gstadt to Frauenchiemsee and Herrenchiemsee islands ... The boat to Herreninsel ... takes 20 minutes

claim: The Altes Schloss Herrenchiemsee (former Augustinian canonry, founded 1130s, dissolved 1803) houses the museum on the 1948 Verfassungskonvent that drafted Germany's Basic Law, plus Ludwig II's bedroom, the Imperial Hall, and a Johann Baptist Zimmermann-painted library.
quote: Museum im Augustiner-Chorherrenstift ... 'Der Wille zur Freiheit und Demokratie – der Verfassungskonvent von Herrenchiemsee 1948' ... Bibliothekssaal ... Johann Baptist Zimmermann

claim: Abtei Frauenwörth on Fraueninsel is a Benedictine convent founded in 772, making it the oldest in Germany still in operation; the three-aisled minster was built around 1100 on 9th-century Carolingian foundations and contains eleven altars and early-Romanesque frescoes.
quote: The nunnery, founded in 772, is the oldest in Germany ... built around the year 1100 on Carolingian foundation walls from the 9th century ... eleven altars, early Romanesque frescoes

claim: Guided 45-minute tours of the Frauenwörth minster by a nun cost €6 per person (€70 for groups up to 12), held weekdays between 11:00 and 13:00 by appointment; church services take precedence.
quote: approximately 45 minutes, meet at the monastery gate, cost 6.00€ per person (or 70.00€ for groups up to 12 people) ... excluding Sundays and holidays

claim: Schloss Hohenaschau in Aschau im Chiemgau is only visitable on a guided tour (May-October); slots run Tue/Thu/Sun/holidays 13:30 & 15:00 and Wed/Fri 10:00 & 11:30; adults €7, children 6-16 €5, family card €15; the steep castle hill needs a 15-20 min uphill walk.
quote: Das Schloss ist nur mit einer Führung zu besichtigen ... Tuesday & Thursday: 1:30 PM & 3:00 PM ... Adults €7.00 ... Allow 15-20 minutes walking uphill

claim: The Falknerei Burg Hohenaschau holds 45-minute raptor flight demonstrations through 18 October 2026 at 11:00 and 15:00; tickets €10 adults / €5 children 5-15 / €28 family, cash only, weather-dependent.
quote: Adults: €10.00, Children (5-15 years): €5.00, Family tickets ... €28.00 ... demonstration lasts approximately 45 minutes ... No card payments are accepted

claim: The Holzknechtmuseum Ruhpolding is open Easter-October, Tue-Sun 10:00-17:00; admission €9 adults, €8 seniors, €7 youth/students to 27, family €20, under-6 free; fully accessible, bilingual German/English, dogs free.
quote: Ostern bis Oktober jeweils Dienstag bis Sonntag, jeweils 10 bis 17 Uhr ... Adults: €9.00 ... Families (up to 2 adults + children): €20.00

claim: The Holzknechtmuseum is a Bezirk-Oberbayern open-air museum recreating the working world of the Chiemgau Holzknechte (woodcutters), with historic huts, sleds, tools and a multimedia journey through forestry history.

Maria Eck above Siegsdorf is the most-visited pilgrimage site in the Archdiocese of Munich-Freising, a 1626 Franciscan monastery and church at 882 m with adjoining Gasthof, frequently combined with a hike from the Eckerwirt parking area.
quote: Maria Eck is a monastery of the Franciscan Minorites from 1626 ... pilgrimage church at 882 meters above sea level is the most well-known pilgrimage church in the Diocese of Munich and Freising

claim: The Maria Klobenstein pilgrimage church lies directly on the Bavarian-Tyrolean border between Schleching and Kössen in the Tiroler-Ache gorge; a Loreto Chapel (1701) and a Mariahilf Chapel (1731-33) were joined into one church in 1890, built around a venerated split rock and spring.
quote: directly on the German-Austrian border between Schleching (Bavaria) and Kössen (Tyrol) ... Loreto Chapel was built in 1701, and the Mariahilf Chapel was built between 1731 and 1733. Since 1890, the two chapels have been structurally connected

claim: The Salinenpark Traunstein, opened 2019 for the city's 400th salt-works anniversary, is a freely accessible open-air museum showing a reconstructed Reiffenstuel pump-wheel and a working 19th-century Reichenbach water-column engine, plus an apothecary garden of ~140 medicinal species.
quote: Salinenpark was opened in 2019 on the occasion of the 400th anniversary of the salt city Traunstein ... reconstruction of the so-called Reiffenstuelpumpe ... original, still functioning Reichenbach water column machine

claim: Inside the Ferdinandistock and Albertistock of the Traunstein Salinen ensemble, an exhibition on the Soleleitung lets visitors take a virtual flight along 'the oldest pipeline in the world', complementing the baroque Salinenkapelle St. Rupert & Maximilian (1630-31).
quote: exhibition has been set up in the Ferdinandistock ... virtual flight journey along the 'oldest pipeline in the world' ... Salinenkapelle St. Rupert and St. Maximilian ... erected between 1630 and 1631

claim: Burg Marquartstein, founded 1075 on a rocky spur above the Tiroler Ache, is the historic core of the Achental; in 1894 Richard Strauss married soprano Pauline de Ahna in the castle church, and the privately owned castle is best appreciated from circular hiking trails (e.g. from Freiweidach).
quote: history as a place begins in 1075 with the construction of Marquartstein Castle ... On September 10, 1894, the famous musician and composer Richard Strauss married his student, the singer Pauline de Ahna, in the castle church

claim: The Salzbergwerk Berchtesgaden (~50 km from Grassau, beyond the strict 30-km radius but a feasible day-trip) offers ~1 h guided underground tours with miner's outfits, two ~40 m slides, a train ride and a raft crossing of an underground brine lake; budget 1.5-2 h on site.
quote: you should allow 1.5 to 2 hours including ticket purchase, dressing, reception and return of miner's clothing. The tour through the world beneath the surface lasts a good hour

claim: Grassau to Aschau im Chiemgau is about 13-14 km by road (≈20-min drive), and Grassau to Ruhpolding about 28 km (≈22 min), placing both squarely within day-trip range.
quote: Grassau - Aschau im Chiemgau driving directions
